answer: The domain in which both the original and the replication studies primarily used student subjects is the **Social** domain. Across the 141 original–replication pairs in the study data, 62 of 74 Social-domain original studies (about 84%) used student subjects and 60 of 74 Social-domain replications (about 81%) used student subjects — the proportions closest to the quoted 82.4% (original) and 80.9% (replication). Student-subject usage was dominant for Social under every pooling of the data (pair-level 83.8%/81.1%; row-level 82.0%/78.4%; per-lab 81.8%/78.1%). No other domain matches: Cognitive studies used student subjects in only about 71–76% of originals (far below 82.4%), and Economics studies exceeded both quoted proportions (94.4% original, 100% replication). Social is therefore the unique domain in which both original and replication studies predominantly used student subjects.
